claims.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys can undergo a temperature-induced partial transformation from bcc to a bcc+hcp microstructure.
The proposed bcc-to-hcp transformation is reversible.
The bcc-to-hcp transformation governs enhanced mechanical strength.
The bcc-to-hcp transformation governs changes in thermoelastic behavior.
The proposed refractory HEA has a predominantly bcc microstructure at room temperature.
Increasing Ta content stabilizes the bcc phase.
Reducing Ta content destabilizes bcc and promotes formation of hcp material within the bcc matrix.
Thermal treatment at 700–1000°C promotes controlled formation of hcp precipitates.
The transformed structure contains nanoscale hcp precipitates embedded in a bcc matrix.
Interfaces between the hcp precipitates and bcc matrix act as heterogeneous sites for elastic response.
The hcp precipitates and their interfaces act as barriers to dislocation motion.
Exposure to service temperatures produces a regionally limited bcc-to-hcp transformation.
The hcp phase has greater resistance to shear than the bcc matrix.
The hcp phase impedes dislocation motion and thereby increases yield strength.
Spatial heterogeneity in the elastic moduli of the bcc and hcp phases alters the bulk thermoelastic response.
Relative to a high-Ta bcc baseline, the lower-Ta dual-phase alloy will have greater yield strength at 700–1000°C.
Relative to a high-Ta bcc baseline, the lower-Ta dual-phase alloy will have a greater elastic modulus at 700–1000°C.
In situ XRD during mechanical loading will show an increasing hcp phase fraction concurrent with the thermoelastic changes.
A high-Ta refractory HEA baseline remains predominantly single-phase bcc under high-temperature conditions.
Controlling grain size and oxygen and nitrogen levels makes the observed property differences directly attributable to phase transformation rather than impurity effects.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis asserts that the transformation is reversible, while the uncertainty field says reversibility under cyclic thermal loading still requires investigation.
